effect: The result explains that placing the mark inside the focal distance produces an upright, enlarged virtual image, unlike the projected image on the screen.
reaction: The contrast between viewing a virtual image and projecting one made the lens result more informative.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lens to light paths was most worthwhile: it explained the placement condition and distinguished a virtual image from a projection.

leastWorthwhile.text: Shaping the glass into a lens was the least engaging passage; it established the object but initially left the useful distance unspecified.

surprise.text: The close-up view is upright and virtual, in contrast to the inverted image on the screen.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the lens combinations were the only offered actions at their respective steps, so there was little meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrast between projection and magnification made the light-path ideas concrete, though I would hope for more decisions than the final two offered.
